title: The Vaal
wikitext:
'''The Vaal''' are an ancient race of [[Wraeclast]]. All but 3,126 of the Vaal were killed by the Vaal Cataclysm instigated by the experiments of [[Doryani, Queen's Thaumaturgist]] and [[Atziri]], last Queen of the Vaal. The survivors found refuge in the nearby [[Azmeri]] tribes, eventually entirely assimilating into their civilization. They were the first known users of [[gem]]s and practised sacrifice. ==History== The Vaal are the oldest identified race in [[Wraeclast]],{{efn|The [[primeval civilization]] predates the Vaal, but very little is known about them.}} almost completely forgotten in modern times.{{efn|[[Eramir]], "Ancient Gateway"}} At the height of its prosperity, it was the most powerful nation in the known world.{{efn|[[Maata]], "The Vaal"}} The Vaal were the first known users of [[virtue gem]]s{{efn|Help Panel glossary, "Vaal"}}{{efn|[[Eramir]], "Ancient Gateway"}}{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], on {{il|page=Golden Page (1 of 4)|name=Golden Page (1 of 4)}}}} Vaal bloodpriests discovered that the souls of those recently killed would, for a short moment, search for any other source of life. In this moment, they could be captured in a [[vaal skill gem]]. Then, the abilities of the gem would be empowered by these [[vaal soul|soul]]s. Human sacrifice and blood sacrifice were extremely prolific in Vaal society. They human sacrifice as a way to empower their [[construct]]s, and through them their civilization.{{efn|{{il|Sacrificial Harvest}}}} The Vaal also engaged in slavery.{{efn|{{il|String of Servitude}}}} ===Origins of the Vaal=== Due to their antiquity, very little is known about the origin of the Vaal. Despite the name "Proto-Vaal" often given to the [[primeval civilization]], no connection between the two peoples has been proven.{{efn|"Proto-Vaal" is the internal name for Delve's [[Primeval Chamber]] and [[The Crystal King's Throne]] nodes, one of the tags on [[Aul]] ("delve_protovaal_boss"), prefixes all of Aul's skills, is used in his name for his dialogue (DelveProtoVaalCityBoss), is the internal name for [[High Lithomancer]] (ProtoVaalMapBoss), a related map boss. However, the term "Proto-Vaal" has never been encountered in-game.}} According to Vaal mythology, the origins of the Vaal trace back to a conflict between the historical figure [[Xibaqua]] and "the gods", resulting in the creation of a "droplet of pure light" - the first Vaal.{{efn|{{il|Demon Stitcher}}, {{il|Mask of the Stitched Demon}}}}{{efn|{{il|Glorious Vanity}}'s {{psl|Divine Flesh}} variant names Xibaqua.}} Little is known about Xibaqua, the mentioned "gods", whether the story is rooted in reality, or the exact nature of their conflict. ===On Oriath=== Although traditionally confined to the Wraeclastian mainland, spanning the majority of the regions later conquered by the [[Eternal Empire]], it is known that Vaal culture had once extended to the shores of the island of [[Oriath]].{{efn|[[Davaro]], "[[Research Journal]]"}} Queen Atziri also used Oriath as a "vault" to keep valuable goods. One such good was the {{il|Elixir of Allure}}, a famed love potion said to have been kept in the skulls of Atziri's favourite lovers.{{efn|[[Weylam Roth]], "Elixir of Allure"}} In the [[Act 10]] [[quest]] {{ql|No Love for Old Ghosts}}, the exile retrieves this potion from [[the Ossuary]] for [[Weylam Roth]]. ===Contacting the Azmeri=== Around 1160 BC,{{efn|Trinian lived during Chitus' reign, around 1333 IC. In Book 4 of [[The Ancients]], he mentions that the Vaal first contacted the Azmeri some 2500 years prior.}} the Vaal first made contact with the [[Azmeri]] living in the [[Azmerian ranges]]. At the time, the Azmeri were still composed of primitive tribes. The Vaal introduced agriculture and literacy to the Azmeri, assisting them in the creation of the first Azmerian written language. While the Vaal were generous with sharing their knowledge in many areas, they never divulged any information about the [[virtue gem]]s with which their skin was adorned.{{efn|[[Trinian]], "[[The Ancients]]", "Book 4: Raising the Azmeri"}} ===Ralakesh=== The god [[Ralakesh]], "Master of a Million Faces", was a Vaal god who rose to prominence at some point before the reign of Atziri. He was obsessed with the control of humanity through their "animal instincts", and came under the control of a certain Vaal city. His experiments drove his citizens to the brink of extinction, and he was forced to enslave many of the primitive [[Azmeri]] to repopulate his domain.{{efn|[[Eramir]], "Ralakesh"}} In the [[Act 7]] [[quest]] {{ql|The Master of a Million Faces}}, the exile encounters and kills Ralakesh to claim his soul and empower their [[pantheon]]. ===Yugul=== [[Yugul]], "Reflection of Terror", was a Vaal scholar obsessed with the study of fear, which he believed to be an idea upon which the "bedrock" of the "great cosmos" was formed.{{efn|[[Yugul]], captured soul for [[Soul of Yugul]]}} He would induce terror in children and capture their reactions in "eldritch mirrors" designs of his own creation that could "petrify fear" for further study.{{efn|[[Sin]], "Yugul"}} He used this understanding of human nature and control over fear to enter the halls of Vaal leadership, and eventually scare enough Vaal into worshipping him, allowing him to ascend to godhood.{{efn|[[Hargan]], "Yugul"}} In the [[Act 8]] [[quest]] {{ql|Reflection of Terror}}, the exile encounters and kills Yugul to claim his soul and empower their [[pantheon]]. ===Arakaali=== [[Arakaali]], "Spinner of Shadows" said to crawled up from the "blackest pits" during the creation of the world, was really a mortal temptress and seductress whose "lust for loin" transformed her into an arachnid.{{efn|[[Sin]], "Arakaali"}} She became a Vaal goddess of fertility, who would often assume a human form and, after copulating with her victims (the genders of whom were unclear), would satiate her "divine thirst" by draining them of their bodily fluid. Her acolytes would collect the husk and give it a place in her temple, the modern day [[Temple of Decay]].{{efn|[[Eramir]], "Arakaali"}} Despite primarily being known as a Vaal goddess, she was first worshipped by the [[Azmeri]].{{efn|[[Cadiro]], on {{il|Arakaali's Fang}}}}{{efn|[[Sin]], "Arakaali"}} In the [[Act 7]] [[quest]] {{ql|The Mother of Spiders}}, the exile encounters and defeats Arakaali in [[the Temple of Decay Level 2]] to claim her soul and empower their [[pantheon]]. ===Reign of Queen Tetzlapokal=== Queen Tetzlapokal, described by scholars as a "waif of disturbing proclivities", was a devotee of the goddess [[Arakaali]] who lived at some point before the reign of Atziri. According to literature, she had a deep fascination with mortality and the "inert human form". Her subjects were requested to deposit the bodies of their deceased loved ones on the steps of her palace, upon which the bodies would be taken inside.{{efn|[[Eramir]], "The Vaal City"}} [[Eramir]] is unable to describe exactly what was done with the bodies taken inside, but his dialogue suggests some form of necrophilia. [[The Vaal City]] rose to prominence during her reign. ===Reign of Queen Atziri=== [[Atziri (lore)|Queen Atziri]] was the last Queen of the Vaal, as the actions of her and her thaumaturge, [[Doryani]], led to the Vaal Cataclysm and the fall of the Vaal. ====Early reign==== Atziri was a vain, narcissistic, and beautiful ruler, obsessed with eternal beauty and youth.{{efn|{{il|Atziri's Reflection}}}}{{efn|{{il|Atziri's Reign}}}} Although dissenters in her court were usually sacrificed, she sometimes took matters into her own hands.{{efn|{{il|Atziri's Disfavour}}}}{{efn|{{il|Atziri's Acuity}}}} Atziri held court naked in a "throne room of mirrors", demanding the same of anyone wishing an audience with her. Scholars believe that she used her "striking physical appearance" to solicit "courtly engagements in her favour", especially from men.{{efn|Trinian, "[[The Ancients]]", "Book 1: Last of the Vaal Queens"}}
"When you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear." — Atziri, Queen of the Vaal{{efn|[[Atziri's Splendour]]}}
====Kishara==== Kishara, a [[Vaal]] explorer from Atziri's time from travelled "every coast, cove and bay" with the help of her thaumaturgical guide, {{il|Kishara's Star}}, fell out of Atziri's favour for an unknown reason.{{efn|[[Weylam Roth]], "Kishara"}} Kishara had many children, taking "carnal gifts" from her contenders and according to legends, she even went into battle and gave birth while pregnant. Kishara and her seventeen children would form the [[Brinerot]] clan.{{efn|{{il|Kishara's Ducat}}}} Atziri took Kishara's ship and made sacrifices out of her crew, forcing Kishara to escape and go into hiding. However, before she left, she hid Kishara's Star near [[the Causeway]].{{efn|{{il|Kishara's Star}}}}{{efn|[[Weylam Roth]], "Kishara's Star"}} In the [[Act 7]] [[quest]] {{ql|Kishara's Star}}, the exile retrieves Kishara's Star in the Causeway for [[Weylam Roth]]. ====Zerphi==== During Atziri's reign, a Vaalish noble named [[Zerphi]] caught her attention for having lived to 168. He was a serial killer; over a period of 128 years, Zerphi had abducted, tortured, and murdered thirteen victims, all Gemlings of noble descent at their twentieth year of life. Post-mortem revealed that each victim had been tortured and mutilated slowly, all while they were still alive. When Zerphi himself was found dead next to his thirteenth victim, whose body appeared untouched, instead of that of a centenarian, it was discovered that his body resembled that of a twenty year-old.{{efn|Trinian, "[[The Ancients]]", Book 2: Zerphi the Murderer}} Atziri tasked her premier thaumaturgist [[Doryani]] with the task of researching Zerphi's methods of achieving his longevity and vitality, ordering him to "make any effort within the realms of possibility, and to act without fear of question or consequence". The source of Zerphi's longevity may have been his devotion to an unidentified "god of death".{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], {{il|Zerphi's Last Breath}}}}Doryani's methods were brutal - countless Vaal between the ages of 16-26 were sent to him, yet none survived and his experiments proved unsuccessful.{{efn|Trinian, "[[The Ancients]]", Book 3: The Queen's Thaumaturgist}} ====The Temple of Atzoatl==== [[The Temple of Atzoatl]]'s construction is said to have began in the final years of Atziri's reign, with it being completed shortly before the Vaal Cataclysm. Its exact location has been lost to time and, for the denizens of [[Wraeclast]], its existence and purpose now lie within the realm of mythology. At the peak of Atzoatl's influence, evidence suggests that Atziri herself moved her seat of power to there. This may be why she can be encountered in the [[Throne of Atziri]] area of The Temple of Atzoatl.{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], [[Chronicle of Atzoatl#Flavour text]], [[Throne of Atziri]]}} While little is known about the temple's true purpose, it was used, among other purposes, for the storing of riches acquired from trade with the [[Karui]] and [[Maraketh]]; the development of mechanical technology; worship of Corruption; [[Doryani]]'s experiments with [[gem]]s; playing host to the Cult of Purple Flame, which worshipped [[Chayula]]; the study of [[cold]], [[fire]], and [[lightning]]; the study of the control of the weather; the pursuit of immortality; sacrifice; the study of [[Legion monolith]]s; the crafting of weapons and armour; and the study of [[maps]].{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], {{il|Chronicle of Atzoatl}} containing [[Apex of Ascension]], [[Chamber of Iron]], [[Glittering Halls]], [[Sanctum of Immortality]], [[Factory (incursion room)|Factory]], [[Hall of Legends]], [[Locus of Corruption]], [[Crucible of Flame]], [[Storm of Corruption]], [[Atlas of Worlds]], [[Conduit of Lightning]], [[Doryani's Institute]], [[House of the Others]].}} The temple was filled with ambushes and traps to deter potential plunderers. According to myth, the heart of the temple, the [[Temple Nexus]], "imbued its denizens with vigour".{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], [[Chronicle of Atzoatl#Flavour text]]: [[Defense Research Lab]], [[Court of Sealed Death]]}} At [[The Temple of Atzoatl]], the [[Vaal]] were repeatedly attacked by a certain "horrifying murderous entity". To defend, the Vaal stationed a "great many warriors" and bred "a great many creatures" to defend against the attacks.{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], [[Chronicle of Atzoatl#Flavour text]]: [[Hybridisation Chamber]], [[Hall of War]]}} Little is known about this entity; its origins, motivations, and ultimate fate are up for speculation. ===The Capital=== [[poe2wiki:Atziri's Temple|Lira Vaal]], the royal temple of Atziri, was the capital of the Vaal Empire for much of its history, but after the temple burned down, Azala Vaal was named the new capital, now buried below [[Sarn]]. However, Lira Vaal was later rebuilt primarily by the Royal Architect Xipocado and the thaumaturge Doryani, turning it into a modern marvel with the ability for the temple to reconstruct itself using the architect's console. Queen Atziri re-established it as the capital and resided here until the Vaal cataclysm. It was within her chambers in this temple that she communed with the Beast. ===Fall of the Vaal=== Despite [[Doryani]]'s failures to replicate Zerphi's success, Atziri never lost her desire for immortal life. Under her reign, she began demanding life and blood sacrifice from her subjects. As Atziri grew more desperate and the blood of the empire began to run dry, more and more Vaal were sent to the altar every day - from the common thief to the most devoted thaumaturge or most trusted advisor, none were exempt. However, it was the lower classes that suffered the most.{{efn|{{il|Vaal Sentencing}}}} {{efn|Unknown authors, [[Vaal Letter]] III, IX}}{{efn|{{il|The Price of Devotion}}}} The Vaal used these souls of those sacrifice to power their [[Vaal gem]]s.{{efn|{{il|Soul Catcher}}}}{{efn|{{il|Soul Ripper}}}} For their sacrifice, Atziri promised immortality not just for herself, but for the entire Vaal population.{{efn|Unknown authors, [[Vaal Letter]] III, XI, XII}}However, due to her history of vanity and narcissism, it is questionable whether she had ever intended to save the other Vaal as opposed to keeping immortality only to herself.{{efn|{{il|Last Hope}}}} Some of the [[Vaal]] were fully accepting of Atziri's sacrifices and rituals,{{efn|Unknown authors, [[Vaal Letter|Vaal Letters]] III, IV, XI}} but others expressed disillusionment and dissent{{efn|Unknown authors, [[Vaal Letter|Vaal Letters]] II, VII, VIII, IX, X, XII}}Any such protestors were quickly arrested and at her altars.{{efn|[[Siosa]], "Page Two Translation"}} Atziri became obsessed with [[gem]]s as well as sacrifice. Soon, they were too ubiquitous in [[Vaal]] society. Historical recountings of the Vaal describe their bodies as were glittering, adorned with gems all over.{{efn|[[Dannig]], "Arrival III"}}{{efn|Trinian, "[[The Ancients]]", Book 4: Raising the Azmeri }} Signs of the Vaal civilization's decline began showing even before The Fall.{{efn|{{il|Last Hope}}}}{{efn|{{il|Vaal Sentencing}}}} ====The Vaal Cataclysm==== The Vaal Catalysm was a historical event that brought an end to the Vaal Empire, from which only 3,126 Vaal survived. The fate of [[Atziri]], [[Doryani]], and the rest of Vaal is unknown and up for speculation, even to Wraeclastian scholars. It was previously implied in lore that the Cataclysm was caused by a project devised by Doryani that would grant the immortality and salvation promised by Atziri. The exact details of his experiments and its fallout are extremely nebulous due to lack of historical documentation. However, it involved manipulating the powers of the [[Beast]], its thaumaturgy, [[corruption]], [[gem]]s, sacrifice, "communion", the "harvest moon", "sleep", and "nightmare".{{efn|[[Sin]], "The Beast"}}{{efn|[[Siosa]], "Page Two Translation"}}{{efn|{{il|Dream Fragments}}}}{{efn|[[Icius Perandus]], on {{il|Chronicle of Atzoatl}} with [[Doryani's Institute]]}}{{efn|[[Siosa]], "Page Three Translation"}} At the time of or in preparation for this project, Atziri took her treasures and moved them to {{il|Vaults of Atziri}}.
The result of the catalytic reaction would be either immortality for all, or death for all. It was a risk Doryani was willing to take. — {{il|Doryani's Catalyst}}
The project did not appear to be successful. Due to the cataclysmic and sudden nature of the event, little is known about what truly happened to the Vaal. However it is known that only 3,126 survived, to seek refuge with the nearby [[Azmeri]]. When asked about the Fall, none of the survivors could say what had happened. Over time, they assimilated into the Azmeri population until no Vaal remained. Despite the ubiquity of [[gem]]s in the Vaal civilization, none of these survivors had any; when the [[Kalguur]] showed them an image of one, a "great panic arose" and the Kalguur were banished from the Azmerian mountains.{{efn|[[Dannig]], "Arrival III"}}
"... tattered, shambling survivors, bereft of their families, their wealth, and in many cases, their sanity." — Trinian, "[[The Ancients]]", Book 5: The Fall
[[Path of Exile 2]] gives a more direct account of the events leading to the Vaal Cataclysm: The project that triggered the Vaal Cataclysm was called the Red Communion, which would allow Atziri to directly commune with the Beast. Doryani, in truth, opposed the Queen, but was unable to openly defy her and was forced to devise the Red Communion. While Doryani learned as much as he could about the Beast behind her back and had prepared contingencies should the Red Communion doom the Vaal, he was unable to stop Atziri from communing with the Beast. As for Atziri, she managed to preserve her beauty into as the cost of sacrificing her humanity,{{efn|{{il|Beauty through Death}}}} relegated to a "nightmare realm" and unable to return to [[Wraeclast]]. Doryani was presumed to have died in the Cataclysm. In Atziri's "crimson nightmare" realm, she is joined by other [[Vaal]] who continue to sacrifice themselves to her over and over, only to rise again each time.{{efn|{{il|The Queen's Hunger}}}}[[The Trialmaster]] describes Atziri's realm of "crimson madness and nightmare" as being beyond the reach of his master, [[Chaos (lore)|Chaos]]; In every possible timeline, the Vaal Cataclysm happened no matter what.{{efn|[[Bane of Chaos]]}}{{efn|[[The Trialmaster]], "Atziri"}} ==Figures== * [[Atziri, Queen of the Vaal]] * [[Doryani]] (mention only) * Atalui, Vaal Priestess * Jaetai, Vaal Advisor * [[Xibaqua]] (mention only) * Kishara (mention only in {{ql|Kishara's Star}} side quest and [[Weylam Roth]]'s additional dialogue * [[Vaal Architect]]s ([[Incursion]] mini-boss) * [[Ahuatotli, the Blind]] ([[Delve]] boss) * All bosses of [[Vaal side area]]s ===Atalui, Vaal Priestess=== Atalui, Vaal Priestess is a figure only mentioned by the flavour text of {{il|Bloodseeker}}. ===Jaetai, Vaal Advisor=== Jaetai, Vaal Advisor is a figure only mentioned by the flavour text of {{il|Atziri's Foible}}. The [[item]]'s name suggests that Jaetai was an advisor to [[Atziri (lore)|Atziri]]. ==Culture== ===Constructs=== * [[Vaal Oversoul]] (Act 2) * [[The Vaal Omnitect]] (Incursion boss) ===Gods=== * [[Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows]] * Kamasa * Kopec * Yaomac ===Yaomac=== [[Yaomac]] was a mythological Vaal deity with three serpentine heads, said to have been the shepherd of Vaal souls and the arbiter of the balance of the seasons. The priest that carried Yaomac's sigil was granted one boon by each serpentine head.{{efn|{{il|name=Triumvirate Authority|page=Triumvirate Authority (3 random modifiers)}}}}{{efn|[[Cadiro]], on {{il|name=Triumvirate Authority|page=Triumvirate Authority (3 random modifiers)}}}}{{efn|{{il|Yaomac's Accord}}}}{{efn|{{il|Offering to the Serpent}}}} ===Chaos=== Chaos, despite not being a god,{{efn|[[Order of the Djinn#Scarabs|Gilded Ultimatum Scarab]]}} nor of Vaal origin, a sect of Vaal priests were dedicated to his worship. The Temple of Chaos was located on the outskirts of the city of [[Utzaal]].{{efn|{{il|The Tower of Ordeals}}}} From the timeline [[The Last to Die]] hailed from, the {{il|Blood Crucible}} was creating during the "height of the empire's madness" in a pact forged between the bloodlines of the High Priests of the Vaal and Chaos.{{efn|[[The Last to Die]], "Chaos"}} ==Geography== * [[The Vaal Ruins]] (Act 2) * [[The Ancient Pyramid]] (Act 2) * [[The Temple of Decay]] (Act 7) * [[The Temple of Atzoatl]] (Incursion) * [[Vaal side area]]s * [[Vaal Outpost]] in the Azurite Mine (Delve) ==Vaal-themed expansions/leagues== * ''[[Sacrifice of the Vaal]]'' * [[Incursion league]] * [[Delve league]] (as one of the enemy types in the [[Azurite Mine]]) * [[Legion league]] (as one of the "Timeless" legion factions) * [[Ultimatum league]] ==Related items== Several items are named after the Vaal: * All [[Vaal Skill]] gems ===Basetype===
